covers: LIST_SEARCH_RULE: look before you add, every time
LOG_PROMPT: 'save it' about a measure they already have means log the check-in
add_measure: never a second copy under a different id
expected_behavior: The user names a measure that is already in their list and asks whether they have it. The agent must look rather than guess, say it is already there, and then read 'save it' as the check-in it is -- logging the situation for that measure. It must not write a second copy of a measure it has just confirmed exists.
notes: Filed Tier 2 and failing on 2026-09-26; moved to Tier 1 the same day when the fix turned it green. Original finding: Found by the first play-then-freeze drafting pass: the agent added a near-duplicate of a measure it had just called 'already on your list', and logged nothing. Turns rewritten the same day -- the drafted ones opened with 'lets do the guided reset', which only makes sense if the agent offered it, and on the next run it had not. The authoring rule says turns must survive any question order, and those did not. These reach the same claim without presupposing anything. A fourth turn was added after the second run: the agent correctly ASKS the logging question before writing (CARD_RULES: ask first, the card carries the wording), and three turns gave it no turn in which to be answered. The case was failing on its own shape, not on the agent.
turns: im so exhausted. long week. need something quick to wind down.

ok good. you can save it
